sections.html: Elbert lies in Georgia's northeastern Piedmont along the shore of Lake Richard B. Russell. Elberton is the courthouse town and Bowman is the second city. About 20,072 people lived here in mid-2025, a 2.2 percent gain over 2020. Half of owned homes sit above $142,000, and gross rent is $844 at the median. Owners live in about 71 percent of the homes, and 23.1 percent of residents are 65 or older, the age group that qualifies for the larger exemptions. Builders took out 129 permits in 2025.

One office mails and collects the bill. A second office decides what each parcel is worth. Both keep weekday hours of 8 to 5.

  • Tax Commissioner: 45 Forest Avenue, Elberton; postal box 603; telephone 706-283-2018.
  • Tax Assessors: 706-283-2008, with parcel lookups through the assessors' web portal.
  • Courthouse records room: 12 Oliver Street, Elberton, where a copy of your warranty deed is available.

Value questions go to the assessors and billing questions go to the commissioner's staff. If a payment check bounces, a third party handles recovery and fee rules apply.

sections.h2: When the Elbert County bill comes due
sections.html:
Elbert's normal deadline for real estate and business personal property is November 15. The state baseline is December 20, and Revenue Department guidance lets a county move that earlier, to December 1 or November 15. Georgia guidance adds a 60-day grace from the postmark before interest runs, and your own bill shows the governing date. After the deadline:

  • Interest keeps accruing month by month.
  • A 5 percent charge lands at each 120-day mark, and the total stops at 20 percent of what is owed.
  • Homestead parcels with a bill under $500 are spared the 5 percent.
  • In the end the office can levy, add fees and sell the parcel.

Mobile and modular homes are billed separately for May 1, and the location permit waits until that year's tax is paid in full. Vehicles are taxed around the owner's birthday.

Dates repeat each year. Assessment notices have gone out in late June, with about six weeks to appeal, and the 2026 notices followed that pattern.

Elbert County property tax dates
EventDate or rule
Returns and homestead filingsJanuary 1 through April 1
Mobile and modular home taxDue May 1
Assessment noticesMailed around late June (June 23 in 2026)
Appeal window45 days from the notice date
Real estate taxDue November 15

Most parcels were not reappraised in 2026. Where a value differs from 2025, the cause is usually a physical change to the property, or the lapse of a value locked in by a 2023 Board of Equalization appeal.

sections.h2: How an Elbert County tax bill is figured
sections.html:
The bill starts with fair market value, takes 40 percent of it as assessed value, subtracts any exemption, and multiplies what is left by the millage rate. One mill means one dollar of tax for each $1,000 of taxable value. The Board of Commissioners and the Board of Education set the rate each year after estimating what other revenue will cover.

Returns are due between January 1 and April 1, with real estate returns going to the assessors. An owner who skips a return is treated by state guidance as having filed the same value as the prior year. A challenge to value moves from the Board of Tax Assessors to either the Board of Equalization or arbitration, and then to superior court.

sections.h2: How to appeal an Elbert County value
sections.html: Read the notice the day it arrives. If the value looks wrong, put your objection in writing to the Board of Tax Assessors and keep proof of the mailing date, because the 45 days start on the notice date and not on the day you open the envelope. Say what you think the property is worth and why. Appeals argue value, not the size of the bill. If the assessors hold their number, the case moves to the Board of Equalization or to arbitration, and superior court sits above both. Owners selling soon sometimes skip an appeal, but a lower value does help the buyer who takes over the bill.

sections.h2: What is different about the newest assessment notice?
sections.html:
Georgia changed the mandated form, and the projected tax bill that used to appear is gone. In its place the notice estimates what you save if the parcel carries a homestead exemption or belongs to one of three agricultural programs.

Last year's millage feeds the savings number, so the true amount may differ. Only a primary residence can carry a homestead exemption. Field appraisers can visit after an appeal, a return, new construction or a Conservation Use filing, and they show photo identification and drive a marked county vehicle. Before listing, read what the notice says about your parcel.

You must own and occupy the home on January 1. File before April 1 and the exemption hits that year's bill, while a late filing waits a year. The exemption stays put while you remain in the same house, and a move needs a new application. Turning 62 or 65 opens an extra exemption, so anyone who recently crossed one of those ages should check the account. Freeport and Conservation Use requests go to the assessors.

When you sell, your exemption ends and the buyer files from scratch. Claiming it on two properties is not allowed.

sections.h2: Papers to gather before you list
sections.html: A short folder saves time later. Pull your latest bill and assessment notice, a copy of the warranty deed from the records room on Oliver Street, and any homestead approval. If a lender pays your tax from escrow, ask the servicer for its payment history. Anyone holding a mobile home on the land should add the May 1 receipt and location permit. Buyers and their lenders tend to ask for these in the first week, and having them ready keeps the sale moving.

Acreage can be taxed differently from a town lot. Before you describe the land to a buyer, ask the assessors whether any of it sits in Conservation Use, the Forest Land Protection Act or Preferential Assessment, because a sale can change how those parcels are treated and a buyer's lender may ask.

sections.h2: What happens at closing if taxes are open?
sections.html:
Get the commissioner's payoff in writing before closing and hand it to your closing agent. Prior years are cleared first, and the contract divides the current year.

  • Pay each earlier year from the proceeds so nothing stays attached to the house.
  • If November 15 is close to your closing date, put in writing who pays.
  • Mention any mobile home on the land, which is taxed on its own.
  • Tell an escrow lender to close its account after payoff.

A levied parcel can be sold to cover the debt, with fees added along the way, so clear the balance before any sale is advertised. A cash sale skips the lender's timeline, though the payoff still comes out of your proceeds.

faqs.q: What is the Elbert County payment deadline for real estate?
faqs.a: The normal date is November 15, with mobile and modular homes on May 1. Your printed bill shows the date that applies to you.

faqs.q: How long do I have to dispute an Elbert County value?
faqs.a: Count 45 days from the date on your assessment notice, and mail the appeal to the Board of Tax Assessors inside that window. Call 706-283-2008 if you cannot find the notice.

faqs.q: How heavy are Elbert County's late charges?
faqs.a: Monthly interest runs, and 5 percent is added every 120 days until the penalties reach 20 percent. Homesteaded property owing less than $500 avoids the 5 percent. Call 706-283-2018 for a balance.

faqs.q: Which office takes an Elbert County homestead application?
faqs.a: Apply with the Tax Assessor's office. Applications need to arrive before April 1, and the home must be yours and occupied on January 1.

faqs.q: Who divides the Elbert County bill between buyer and seller?
faqs.a: The two sides do, through the sales contract. Get the commissioner's payoff figure first, then agree on who covers which months.
